sections.heading: Planning your River Modern interior
sections.text:
District 9 homes are often bought for their position in the city: close to work, close to the river, close to the Orchard belt. The interior brief that usually follows is compact and exacting. Circulation has to stay clear, storage has to be built in rather than piled, and the kitchen — frequently open or partly open to dining — has to look finished from the sofa. That is why Maison starts with carpentry: an entry cabinet that actually takes shoes and bags, a living-room joinery wall, handleless kitchen cabinets with a tall pantry, and full-height wardrobes in every bedroom that needs one. We do not use loose, flat-pack furniture as the main look. In a city apartment, a close photograph of a counter, a wardrobe interior or a fluted panel is often as useful as a wide corner-to-corner view.

We have no official floor plan on file and will not invent typologies or a typical square footage. River views, city views or a walk to any particular station are marketing claims until you check your own stack, floor and facing on the key plan. Plan blinds, glare control and any window bench around the outlook you actually have, and read the management rules before you change a balcony.

Orchard Sophia, Duet @ Emily, One Leonie Residences and CanningHill Piers are other Maison pages in or next to this district; use them as internal references, not as a substitute for your own plan. When keys are in sight, the sequence is defects, measurement, renovation approval, then works. A moderate carpentry scope is often planned at about six to ten weeks on site after approvals — an editorial allowance, not a promise. WhatsApp Maison with your approved plan when you are ready.
